segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones, temporary residents of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through being made holy by the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy gave us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who are being guarded by God’s power through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if it must be, you have been grieved by various trials,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes yet is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Though you have not seen him, you love him; though you do not see him now, you believe in him and rejoice with a joy that is beyond words and filled with glory,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as you receive the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied about the grace meant for you inquired and searched carefully,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: searching for what time or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ within them was pointing to when testifying in advance to the sufferings destined for Christ and the glories that would follow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in these things, which have now been announced to you through those who brought you the good news by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things into which angels long to look.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, with your minds belted for action and staying sober, set your hope fully on the grace being brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As children of obedience, do not conform to the desires you had before, in your ignorance,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but, as the one who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in your whole way of life,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it is written,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “You shall be holy, because I am holy.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if you call on as Father the one who judges impartially according to each person’s work, live the time of your stay as foreigners in fear,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: knowing that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were ransomed from the futile way of life handed down from your ancestors,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was foreknown before the foundation of the world, but was made manifest at the end of the times for the sake of you

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now that you have purified your souls by obedience to the truth, leading to sincere love for your brothers and sisters, love one another earnestly from the heart,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: since you have been given new birth, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: but the word of the Lord endures forever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And this is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.

notes.note: The word describes someone staying for a time in a place that is not their home, a visiting foreigner without local citizenship. ‘Exiles’, used by several modern translations, suggests banishment, which the Greek does not say; ‘sojourners’ is accurate but no longer current English. Verse 17 uses a related term for living as a resident foreigner. Whether the label describes the readers’ actual social status, their spiritual situation, or both is debated.

This was the established term, taken from the Greek Old Testament, for Jews living scattered among the nations outside the land of Israel. The letter applies Israel’s vocabulary to its readers, many of whom appear from later verses to have been Gentiles.

The pairing of obedience with sprinkled blood recalls the covenant ceremony of Exodus 24, where the people pledged obedience and Moses sprinkled them with the blood of the sacrifice. Most interpreters see that scene behind the phrase, so that the readers are pictured as brought into a covenant through the death of Jesus.

The Greek relative can mean ‘in this’ (the whole situation just described), ‘in which’ (the last time, making the rejoicing future), or ‘in whom’ (God or Christ). The verb form can also be read as a command, ‘rejoice’. Most translations take it as a statement referring to what precedes, as here.

The Greek word covers life, the self, and the inner person; it does not by itself imply an immaterial part separable from the body. Many scholars think that in this letter it means the whole person, so that the phrase could be rendered ‘the salvation of your lives’ or simply ‘your salvation’. The traditional word is kept here and in verse 22.

notes.phrase: what time or what kind of time
notes.note: The Greek can be read either as two questions about the time (‘what time or what sort of time’) or as one about a person and one about the time (‘what person or what time’). Several major translations take the second view. Many grammarians and commentators prefer the first, since both question words most naturally attach to the single noun ‘time’, and it is followed here.

notes.phrase: with your minds belted for action
notes.traditional: gird up the loins of your mind / prepare your minds for action
notes.note: The Greek says literally ‘having girded up the loins of your mind’. People wearing long robes tucked them into a belt before working, running, or travelling, so the expression means getting ready for exertion. It may echo the instruction to eat the Passover with loins girded, ready to leave Egypt.

The adverb stands between ‘being sober’ and ‘set your hope’ and could belong to either: ‘being completely sober, set your hope’ or ‘being sober, set your hope completely’. Most translations take it with ‘hope’, as here, though some commentators argue for the other reading because this author usually places such adverbs after the verb they modify.

The verb means to set free by paying a price, and was used of buying slaves or captives out of bondage; in the Greek Old Testament it describes God freeing Israel from Egypt. ‘Redeemed’ is the older English rendering, but it has become a general religious term and no longer conveys the payment that the mention of silver and gold presupposes. Several modern translations also use ‘ransomed’.

Many manuscripts read ‘from a pure heart’, and a number of translations follow them. The edition translated here reads simply ‘from the heart’, judging that ‘pure’ was added by copyists. The evidence is fairly evenly divided and editors disagree.

notes.phrase: the living and enduring word of God
notes.traditional: the living and abiding word of God
notes.note: Grammatically ‘living and enduring’ could describe either the word or God (‘the word of the living and enduring God’). Most interpreters attach the adjectives to the word, because the quotation that follows says that the word of the Lord endures.

notes.phrase: “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers, and the flower falls,
notes.note: The quotation is Isaiah 40:6–8 in a form close to the ancient Greek translation. ‘Flesh’ here means humanity in its frailty and mortality. In Isaiah the passage announces comfort to exiles, which fits the letter’s picture of its readers as foreigners away from home.

candidates.reason: Ranges over life, self, and soul across the New Testament, and ‘soul’ can import a body–soul dualism the word does not carry; translators split between ‘soul’, ‘life’ and ‘self’.
With πάροικος/παροικία it recurs in 1 Peter, Hebrews and Acts, and is variously rendered exile, stranger, sojourner, foreigner; the choice shapes how readers picture the community.
Means both testing and temptation across the Gospels, James and the letters, and the English must be split consistently by sense.
The λύτρον word group (ransom/redeem/redemption) recurs in the Gospels, Paul, Hebrews and here, and ‘redeem’ versus ‘ransom’ should be decided once.
A key term in 1–2 Peter and elsewhere (with the verb ἀναστρέφω), rendered conduct, behaviour, manner of life or the archaic ‘conversation’; it needs one consistent English equivalent.

warnings: Verse 21: πιστός is not rendered with a register form (faithful / believing) and has no register-exception note.
